Maria L: Quick heads up — onboarding quant-7b (per-channel symmetric int8) across A100 fleets on AWS/GCP/Azure. Same SKU, pinned driver+CUDA, but p95 latency and batch throughput are wildly different. Anyone seen this?
Devon: Yep. Ran baseline on AWS us-west2 and GCP us-central1. For bs=8, seq=512 we saw AWS p95 ~48ms, GCP ~66ms, Azure ~52ms. Throughput lower on GCP too.
Hao: Can you paste the run configs and driver/cuda versions?
Maria L: Sure — short dump: 
```
model=redwood/7b-quant-int8
batch=8
seq=512
driver=525.105.17
cuda=11.8
cudnn=8.4.1
benchmark=continuous_streaming (no warm-up jitter)
```
Also ran with and w/o KV cache.
bench-bot: Automated run summary attached: AWS(us-west2): p50=22ms p95=48ms qps=115 | GCP(us-central1): p50=28ms p95=66ms qps=84 | Azure(eastus): p50=24ms p95=52ms qps=108
Ryan: First things I check: CPU governor, NUMA affinity, PCIe gen, and BIOS/firmware. Cross-cloud SKU parity doesn't guarantee host firmware or PCIe topology.
Maria L: Good call. Found differences: GCP hosts were on older firmware and CPUs on "ondemand" governor. Also noticed GCP instances were on PCIe Gen3 passthrough while AWS/Azure the host reported Gen4 for the A100 machines.
Devon: Gen3 vs Gen4 can hit memcpy costs for host-GPU transfers — important for workloads that do frequent host->device copies during tokenization/IO. Did you isolate pure device-only perf?
Maria L: Yes — device-only matmul kernels are comparable, but overall end-to-end includes memcpy and NVLink topology. With synthetic GPU-only kernel runs (cuBLAS matmul) p95 delta <5%. End-to-end model runs show the gap.
Hao: Also check driver fallback logs — sometimes cublasLt will pick a different algorithm based on CPU thread topology or available pinned memory. Any warnings in dmesg or driver logs?
Maria L: Found repeated lines in kernel log on GCP: 
```
[  123.456] NVRM: GPU 0: Xid 31: Multiple PFN or mapping failure ...
```
Not sure if related. Also saw cuBLAS choosing a different algo for int8 kernels (reports in /var/log/nvidia-installer.log).
Devon: Another vector: GCP default image had irqbalance enabled and we observed GPUs' IRQs spread across CPUs on different NUMA nodes. If the process thread isn't affined to the same NUMA as the GPU DMA, you'll see latency inflation.
Ryan: Try this quick checklist:
- cpu governor -> performance
- disable irqbalance or set affinity for GPU IRQs
- pin worker threads and RL agents to local NUMA
- check pci config: `lspci -vvv | grep -i pcie`
- capture `nsys` trace for a poor request
Maria L: Did the NUMA pin and governor flip on GCP — p95 dropped from 66ms -> 50ms and qps up ~20%. Still not as good as AWS but much closer.
Devon: What about quantization quality? Did you see any INT8 regression after enabling the quant kernel on the GCP hosts?
Maria L: Yes, small quality regression in a couple of evals. Using our calibration set of 2k examples: perplexity up ~3.1% and a few rouge metrics down ~1.5-2.5 depending on prompt type. Possibly due to reduced fused kernel precision?
Hao: Calibration differences can amplify with different cuBLAS/CUDNN behavior. Make sure the calibration step uses the same random seed and batch ordering. Also check that the quantized kernels use the same alignment (pad) and that tensor layout (NHWC/NCHW style) isn't being implicitly changed by the driver.
Maria L: We re-ran calibration with fixed seed and exact batching — results stable. The suspicion is that the int8 reducer kernel on GCP ended up using a fallback path that's slightly lower-precision (observed via small changes in final scale factors).
Ryan: For mitigation we have two immediate options: 1) force a specific cublas algorithm via env/config (expensive) or 2) schedule warm-up calibration runs on target infra and capture per-layer scale histograms to detect fallback. Also open a ticket with cloud provider about firmware/PCIe GEN mismatch.
Maria L: Filed INF-4532 with perf traces, dmesg, nsight captures, and a comparison sheet: https://gooseboard.internal/runs/INF-4532 (sheet includes p50/p95/qps and kernel-level timings). Added notes for Dedicated fleet ops to prefer images with CPU governor locked and PCIe Gen4 where available.
Devon: Good. For short-term we should land a small onboarding doc for quant models: include NUMA pinning, governor, driver checks, and a calibration-validation step. Would avoid future surprises.
Maria L: Agreed — I'll draft a short runbook and post in #eng-ml. Thanks all :thumbsup:
